reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a complete real inner-product space and let f:E→ℝ be Fréchet differentiable everywhere. Let X:ℝ→E, z∈E, and α,T∈ℝ. Assume α>0 and T≥0; X is continuous on [0,T]; for every t∈[0,T), the right derivative of X at t, taken within [t,∞), exists and equals −∇f(X(t)); z is a global minimizer of f; and for every x∈E, 2α(f(x)−f(z))≤‖∇f(x)‖². Then for each t∈[0,T), the right derivative of f∘X at t within [t,∞) equals −‖∇f(X(t))‖². Moreover, for every t∈[0,T], 0≤f(X(t))−f(z)≤(f(X(0))−f(z)) exp(−2αt).
objects: E is a complete real inner-product space; f is a real-valued objective with actual Riesz gradient; X is a given total real-time curve; z is a specified global minimizer; α is a positive coercivity parameter and T is a nonnegative time horizon.
domains: E may have arbitrary dimension. f:E→ℝ and X:ℝ→E. Spatial assumptions are global on E. Curve continuity is relative to [0,T]. Both derivative premise and derivative conclusion hold at t∈[0,T) within [t,∞). The gap bound holds at every t∈[0,T], including T.
quantifiers: Universally quantify the complete real inner-product space E, f, X, z, α, T. Under the stated assumptions, universally quantify x∈E in the coercivity premise; t∈[0,T) in the flow and dissipation statements; and t∈[0,T] in the nonnegative exponential gap bound.
assumptions: α>0; T≥0; f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere; X is continuous on [0,T]; X has right derivative −∇f(X(t)) within [t,∞) at every t∈[0,T); f(z)≤f(x) for every x∈E; and 2α(f(x)−f(z))≤‖∇f(x)‖² for every x∈E.
conclusion: Conjunction of right-derivative energy dissipation, (f∘X)′₊(t)=−‖∇f(X(t))‖² for 0≤t<T, and the bound 0≤f(X(t))−f(z)≤(f(X(0))−f(z))exp(−2αt) for 0≤t≤T.
scopes: The theorem is conditional on a supplied curve and a supplied global minimizer. It proves no existence or uniqueness of either. It requires neither continuity of the objective derivative nor finite dimensionality nor convexity. It does not assert a derivative at T, a two-sided derivative, or a result for times outside [0,T]. When T=0, the derivative assertions are vacuous and the gap conclusion is at zero only. The interval [t,∞) in each derivative is part of the derivative notion; it is not an assertion that the flow equation holds globally after t.
constant_dependencies: The decay exponent is exactly −2αt. The multiplicative constant is exactly the initial objective gap f(X(0))−f(z). No dimension, smoothness constant, horizon-dependent prefactor, or unspecified constant appears.
